Fixed-length baseline

As a sanity-check baseline, we ignore the video content and task instruction entirely. We simply split each episode into consecutive segments that are exactly 5.77s long, the mean gold segment duration in WGO‑Bench, and score the resulting boundaries against the human subtask boundaries. This reaches 0.070 Segment F1 on the full 100-episode benchmark.

Splitting Videos by Similarity

Our first non-trivial approach follows prior work on VLM captioning for subtask segmentation (⁠Suzuki et al., 2026⁠). We ask a VLM (Gemini 3.5 Flash) to caption frames from the video, embed those captions, then split segments when the cosine similarity between neighboring caption embeddings drops far enough. Unfortunately, the threshold suggested in the paper heavily over-segments, and even after sweeping many similarity thresholds this method only barely beats the fixed-length baseline, reaching 0.081 F1.
